title: Technical Interview Sprint
summary: You're 10 minutes into a technical interview. The interviewer just asked you to walk through how you'd approach a problem you've never seen before — not solve it perfectly, just show your thinking.

title: Behavioral Interview (STAR Method)
summary: An interviewer asks: 'Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision at work or school. What did you do?' You have about 90 seconds to answer well.

title: 60-Second Elevator Pitch Challenge
summary: A recruiter you've been hoping to meet just asked, 'So, tell me about yourself.' You have about 60 seconds before they need to move to the next person in line.

title: Difficult Feedback Conversation
summary: A team member has missed the same deadline twice in three weeks, and you have a 1-on-1 with them in 15 minutes. You need to raise it directly without being harsh.

title: Budget Cut Decision Sprint
summary: Your department's budget just got cut by 15% for next quarter. You have four ongoing initiatives and need to decide what to cut, reduce, or protect — before the finance meeting in 20 minutes.

title: Safety Walk Simulation
summary: You're doing a routine safety walk on an active site. You have about 10 minutes to spot hazards before reporting back to the site manager.

title: Scope Creep Conversation
summary: A client asks, mid-call, 'Can you also just quickly add X?' — a request that's outside the original agreed scope and would take real time, but they're framing it as small.

title: Code Review Roleplay
summary: You're reviewing a colleague's code and found a real bug — a function that will fail under certain inputs. You need to leave a comment on it.

title: Root Cause 5-Whys Sprint
summary: A website went down for 20 minutes. The immediate cause was a server running out of memory. Your team lead wants the real root cause before everyone moves on, not just 'the server ran out of memory.'

title: Delegation Decision Sprint
summary: You have a task that needs doing this week: preparing a client-facing summary report. You could do it yourself (30 min, guaranteed quality) or delegate it to a capable but newer team member (they'd need 90 min and some guidance, but it's a good growth opportunity for them).

title: Bid/No-Bid Decision Sprint
summary: A tender opportunity just landed — a project that fits your company's expertise well, but the client has a reputation for slow payment and the tender preparation itself will cost real time and money with no guarantee of winning.

title: AI Prompt Challenge
summary: You need an AI assistant to help draft a professional email to a client about a project delay. Your first prompt attempt got a generic, unhelpful response. You have one more try to get something usable.

title: Client Meeting Simulation
summary: A client opens the call by saying, 'Honestly, I'm not happy. This is the second delay this month.' You need to respond in the next 30 seconds.

title: Objection Handling Roleplay
summary: A prospect says, 'Your price is higher than [competitor]. Why should I pick you?' You have to respond in the moment, live on the call.

title: Executive Summary Sprint
summary: You've just finished a 12-page project report, but the board only reads the 1-page executive summary. You have 10 minutes to write it.

title: Underperformance Decision Sprint
summary: A team member has missed targets for the third consecutive month despite two prior coaching conversations. You need to decide the next step — before your check-in with HR in 20 minutes.

title: Cost Overrun Investigation Sprint
summary: Finance just flagged that your project's spend is 22% over the monthly budget. You have a call with your director in 20 minutes and need to know why before you walk in.

title: Risk Register Sprint
summary: You have 10 minutes in today's check-in to update the project risk register. Three new risks have come up this week and need to be logged and prioritized.

title: Strategic Prioritization Matrix
summary: You have four potential projects for next quarter but capacity for only two. You need to rank them using a clear framework before presenting to leadership in 20 minutes.

title: Hackathon Micro-Challenge
summary: Your company is running an internal hackathon: build a rough concept for reducing customer support response time, in 45 minutes, working solo. You have time for planning, not full execution.

title: Meeting Facilitation Drill
summary: You're facilitating a meeting, and 15 minutes in, the conversation has drifted into an unrelated tangent that two people are debating passionately. You have 15 minutes left and three agenda items still to cover.

title: RFI Review Challenge
summary: Three Requests for Information (RFIs) are sitting in your queue. You have 15 minutes before a site meeting and need to triage which needs an urgent response.

title: NCR Review Sprint
summary: A batch of materials has been flagged as a minor non-conformance — slightly outside spec but arguably usable. You need to decide the disposition before the site team, waiting to proceed, escalates.

title: Drawing Clash Detection Sprint
summary: You're reviewing a federated 3D model before a coordination meeting and need to identify which flagged clashes are real problems worth discussing versus noise.

title: One-on-One Coaching Sprint
summary: A normally engaged team member has seemed quieter and less energetic in the last two weeks. You have your regular weekly 1-on-1 in 5 minutes and want to check in without making it awkward.

title: Sustainability Trade-off Sprint
summary: You're choosing between a standard building material (cheaper, higher carbon footprint) and a sustainable alternative (15% more expensive, significantly lower carbon footprint) for a client who has both budget constraints and stated sustainability goals.

title: Email Triage Sprint
summary: You're back from a few days away and have 47 unread emails. You have 15 minutes before your first meeting to triage the most important ones.
